title: AWS Reference
description: A quick reminder of the ideas and examples in the AWS lessons. Open the linked lesson when you need more help.

entries.name: What AWS provides
entries.summary: Amazon Web Services offers rented computing and storage. You choose services for a job and pay according to their rules and usage.

example.code:
Need: share a static reading page
Possible parts: object storage and a content delivery service
Practice today: draw the plan only

notes: Cloud resources can cost money even while you are learning; this course creates none.

entries.name: Regions and Availability Zones
entries.summary: An AWS Region is a geographic area. It contains separate Availability Zones designed to reduce shared failure risks.

example.code:
Region: eu-west-1
Availability Zone: eu-west-1a
Plan: keep related practice resources in a chosen Region

notes: Do not assume two Zones are the same physical building.

entries.name: Identity and access with IAM
entries.summary: IAM controls who can do what in AWS. A policy grants actions on resources. Least privilege means granting only needed actions.

example.code:
Reader needs: read one approved object
Reader does not need: change account settings or delete a bucket

notes: Do not practise with root-account access or put credentials in source files.

entries.name: S3 objects and buckets
entries.summary: Amazon S3 stores objects inside buckets. An object has a key, which is its name within a bucket. Slashes in keys can look like folders.

example.code:
Bucket: fictional-club-assets
Object key: pages/index.html
Object data: the page file

notes: Do not make a bucket public just to work around an access error.

entries.name: Object access and versioning
entries.summary: S3 access settings decide who can read an object. Versioning can retain earlier versions, but it is separate from access control and backup planning.

example.code:
Object: pages/index.html
Version A: old heading
Version B: corrected heading
Access: remains controlled separately

notes: Turning on versioning does not make an object private automatically.

entries.name: EC2 virtual machines
entries.summary: An EC2 instance is a virtual machine. You choose its size and operating-system image, then remain responsible for much of its software upkeep.

example.code:
Planned instance: small Linux VM
Job: a separate learning experiment
Needed upkeep: updates, permissions and monitoring

notes: Stopping a VM may not remove charges for associated storage or other resources.

entries.name: VPCs and subnets
entries.summary: A Virtual Private Cloud is a network space you configure. A subnet is a range of network addresses inside that VPC and one Availability Zone.

example.code:
VPC range: 10.0.0.0/16
Example subnet: 10.0.1.0/24
Location: one chosen Availability Zone

notes: Do not overlap address ranges without understanding the network consequences.

entries.name: Security groups filter traffic
entries.summary: A security group controls allowed traffic for attached resources. It is stateful: replies to allowed traffic are handled as part of that connection.

example.code:
Example web rule: allow TCP 443 from the intended clients
No rule: unrestricted administration from the whole internet

notes: A security group is not a substitute for patching software and checking application permissions.

entries.name: CloudFront caches content
entries.summary: CloudFront is a content delivery service. It can serve cached copies from edge locations nearer to visitors.

example.code:
Visitor -> nearby edge cache
Cache miss -> approved origin
Response -> visitor

notes: Do not cache private personalised data with public cache rules.

entries.name: CloudWatch observations
entries.summary: CloudWatch provides metrics, logs and alarms for supported resources. A metric is a number over time; an alarm checks a condition.

example.code:
Metric: request errors per minute
Alarm condition: errors exceed the chosen threshold
Response plan: inspect logs and recent changes

notes: Do not collect unnecessary personal data in logs.

entries.name: Budgets are alerts
entries.summary: A budget helps track spending and can notify you when a threshold is reached. An alert is not automatically a hard spending stop.

example.code:
Monthly learning limit: a fictional 5 currency units
Alert threshold: 80 percent
Alert point: 4 units

notes: Read service costs and clean up authorised practice resources; an alert alone does not cap charges.

entries.name: Plan a static site carefully
entries.summary: A cloud design should name the needed services, access rules, costs and cleanup steps. Keep a static learning site as static files.

example.code:
Files: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and images
Access: read-only delivery to visitors
Origin: approved static-file storage
Review: domain, HTTPS, cache rules, cost

notes: Do not deploy a plan until the owner approves the exact resources and cost.
